title: Who is actually responsible?
caption:
When something changes in town, the anger usually lands on the most visible official.

Local power is divided. A city council votes on the city budget. A school district is often a separate government with its own votes.

The Daily Nun traced who decides what, and where the public record of each vote is kept.

reel.title: Who signs the check?
reel.voiceover: Angry about a local decision? Don't tag the mayor. Power is divided. Councils vote on city budgets. School boards often run separately. Find the agenda. Read the minutes. They name who voted. The Daily Nun.

sources.limits: Summarizes California's Brown Act: agenda posted at least 72 hours before a regular meeting, and public comment. A secondary summary, and California only. Notice periods differ in other states.

sources.title: Florida Statutes, section 286.011
sources.author: State of Florida
sources.limits: Requires 'reasonable notice' of meetings and recorded minutes. It sets no fixed number of hours.
